tip: Опавшие (opavshie = fallen) is a past participle used like an adjective, agreeing with листья (listya = leaves) in the plural.
грустно (grustno = sad) with the infinitive смотреть (smotret = to look) means it is sad to look, and needs no subject.
Умывшись (umyvshis = having washed) is a verbal adverb; the -вшись (-vshis) ending marks a completed action done before he sat down.
Выученный (vyuchenny = learned) is a past passive participle used as an adjective, agreeing with урок (urok = lesson).
Будучи (buduchi = being) is the verbal adverb of быть (byt = to be), and the noun after it goes to instrumental: студентом (studentom = student).
было принято (bylo prinyato = was made) is a past passive; было agrees with the neuter Решение (reshenie = decision).
Russian uses the present учу (uchu = I study) with уже полгода (uzhe polgoda = already half a year) where English says I have been studying.
Гуляя (gulyaya = walking) is an imperfective verbal adverb with -я (-ya), showing action at the same time as встретили (vstretili = met).
Идущий (idushchy = walking) is a present active participle, a one-word way to say the man who is walking, agreeing with человек (chelovek = man).
Потеряв (poteryav = having lost) is a perfective verbal adverb; the -в (-v) ending marks an action finished before he kept going.
строится (stroitsya = is being built) adds -ся (-sya) to make the verb passive: the road is being built, with no builder named.
The person sold to takes the dative: новому владельцу (novomu vladeltsu = to the new owner) after была продана (byla prodana = was sold).
Замёрзшее (zamyorzsheye = frozen) is a past participle used like an adjective, agreeing with the neuter озеро (ozero = lake).
To thank for something use за (za) plus the accusative: за обращение (za obrashchenie = for reaching out) after Благодарим (blagodarim = we thank).
In a passive, the doer takes the instrumental: разработана инженерами (razrabotana = developed, inzhenerami = by engineers).
Учась (uchas = studying) is the verbal adverb of the reflexive учиться (uchitsya = to study), keeping the reflexive -сь (-s) ending.
в течение (v techenie = within) takes the genitive: в течение трёх дней (tryokh dney = of three days).
